Synopsis:
    Global bond yields are surging to multi-year highs driven by Middle East conflict pushing oil above $91/bbl, renewed inflation fears, and a hawkish Fed pivot under Chair Kevin Warsh. US 10Y yields broke 4.75% resistance to 4.78%. Markets are pricing rate hikes across the US, Japan, New Zealand, and Europe imminently. Equity sentiment is cautious ahead of Friday's US jobs data. Dollar support is limited as rate rises are globally synchronized.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES (the Fed policy repricing and US Treasury yield breakout are the central driver of the entire article's narrative)

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 95 (strongly YES — a September Fed hike is explicitly called the start of a minimum three-hike cycle)
Probability of increase: 65%

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?

Probability of holding: 20%

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 80 (decidedly MORE HAWKISH — US 10Y has broken key 4.75% resistance, Fed Chair Warsh has reset rate expectations upward, a September hike is better-than-even odds, and a strategist explicitly calls for a minimum three-hike cycle starting now)
